# Remove Trailing Zeros From a String.

@example The last three zeros go; the zero between 9 and 7 stays.
"907000"
=> "907"

@example The last digit is 6, so there is nothing to remove.
"4096"
=> "4096"

@example Thirty digits are too many for any built-in integer type; only the 1 is left.
"100000000000000000000000000000"
=> "1"

# A single digit.
"5"
=> "5"

# Exactly one trailing zero.
"10"
=> "1"

# Zeros only inside the number: nothing to remove.
"1002003"
=> "1002003"

# Zeros inside and at the end: only the ones at the end go.
"100200300"
=> "1002003"

# A zero inside comes before the trailing one, so cutting at the first
# zero from the left would lose the 5.
"6050"
=> "605"

# Two trailing zeros, not just one.
"8800"
=> "88"

# Every digit from 1 to 9, then a zero.
"1234567890"
=> "123456789"

# 2^64 + 4, just past the largest unsigned 64-bit integer.
"18446744073709551620"
=> "1844674407370955162"

# The longest run of trailing zeros: a 9 and then 999 zeros.
""
=> "9"

# 1000 digits and no zero at all: the result is the whole of num, one
# character more than a 1000-byte buffer holds with its NUL.
""
=> ""

# 30 written 300 times, then 400 zeros: the last 401 zeros go, and the
# 299 zeros inside stay.
""
=> ""

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 2 small
"29106"
=> "29106"

@gen 3 small
"6000800"
=> "60008"

@gen 5 small
"202100"
=> "2021"

@gen 6 small
"8067000"
=> "8067"

@gen 12 small
"310"
=> "31"

@gen 16 small
"400"
=> "4"

@gen 19 small
"40787"
=> "40787"

@gen 24 small
"3830520"
=> "383052"

# Full size: 1000 digits, with 259, 0 and 709 trailing zeros.
@gen 1
""
=> ""

@gen 3
""
=> ""

@gen 4
""
=> "724780830603720826822205500080154072639304091292805808058025772906974057907769100092106500790264656696286010653002685591617386517029206311022068837102205200070009084294464556750080905557364000327332560504445407771128075719495990607950086068089146809807900261060529091099584101747610620450777"
